facts.value: The EU's role in basic education is limited to supporting national governments.
The policy for higher education was developed in the 1980s in programmes supporting exchanges and mobility.
The Erasmus Programme is a university exchange programme that began in 1987.
In its first 20 years, the Erasmus Programme supported international exchange opportunities for well over 1.5 million university and college students.
The Lifelong Learning Programme 2007–2013 was designed for school pupils, teachers, trainees in vocational education and training, and adult learners.
The EU supports the Bologna Process to establish comparable standards and compatible degrees across Europe.
The first EU Framework Programme for research started in 1984 to coordinate and stimulate research.
The European Research Council allocates EU funds to European or national research projects.
EU research and technological framework programmes focus on various areas, including developing a diverse mix of renewable energy.
